params.body:
With one post on the site, the news overview was a large heading block, an empty band and a single white card in the left two thirds of the page. The post page had seven sections and no way to see or reach them except by scrolling.

## News overview (`src/pages/news.astro`)

- **The newest story opens the page.** Its cover photo runs from the left edge of the screen, directly under the menu. "News" (the page's `h1`), the date, the title and the summary sit beside it on a pale blue that fades down into the page colour. The blue is the site's own `--blue`, mixed into `--bg`.
- **Older stories follow under "Earlier"**, two across: a small photo, the date, the title, and the summary in small text, cut off after three lines.
- **On a narrow screen** the photo comes first and the text field sits under it; older stories go to one column.
- **No posts:** the heading and the "first updates are on their way" note are kept as they were.
- A post without a cover image gets the text field across the full width; an older story without one gets text only.

## Post page (`src/pages/news/[slug].astro`)

- **"In this story":** the post's section headings as links. On a wide screen the list sits in the free column to the right of the text, stays in view while scrolling, and marks the section being read. On a narrow screen it is a short list under the opening paragraph.
- It appears only when a post has three or more headings.
- Headings get an `id` made from their text at build time. `portableText.js` is untouched.

## Checked

- `npm test`: 25 passed. `npm run build` and `npm run check:built`: no contact number.
- Overview against the live post at 1440 and 390 wide: one `h1`, no horizontal scroll, no page errors. The list of older stories was checked in a local preview with stand-in posts, since Sanity holds one post.
- "In this story" at 1440, 1100 and 390 wide: a click scrolls to the section and the current section is marked.
params.title: News: the newest story opens the overview, and a post lists its sections
